claim: sam35-2 and sen2-1 are temperature-sensitive alleles in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
source: To elucidate how misfolded mitochondrial proteins are targeted for destruction, we exploited two previously-identified yeast ts- alleles, sam35-2 and sen2-1 (Li et al., 2011; Milenkovic et al., 2004; Winey and Culbertson, 1988), whose degradation has not been assessed.
evidence: The text cites previous studies that identified these alleles as temperature-sensitive.

claim: Sam35 is an essential MOM protein.
source: Sam35 and Sen2 are essential MOM proteins.
evidence: The text directly states that Sam35 is an essential mitochondrial outer membrane protein.

claim: Sen2 is an essential MOM protein.
source: Sam35 and Sen2 are essential MOM proteins.
evidence: The text directly states that Sen2 is an essential mitochondrial outer membrane protein.

claim: Sam35 is the substrate receptor of the MOM-embedded multiprotein sorting and assembly machinery (SAM) complex.
source: Sam35 is the substrate receptor of the MOM-embedded multiprotein sorting and assembly machinery (SAM) complex required for assembly of β-barrel proteins into the MOM (Chan and Lithgow, 2008; Kozjak et al., 2003; Kutik et al., 2008; Milenkovic et al., 2004).
evidence: The text cites multiple studies establishing Sam35's role as the substrate receptor of the SAM complex.

claim: Sam35 is tightly embedded at the MOM via the Sam50 protein.
source: Although Sam35 contains no apparent membrane spans, it is tightly embedded at the MOM via the Sam50 protein (Kutik et al., 2008).
evidence: The text cites a study showing Sam35's association with the MOM through Sam50.

claim: Sen2 provides endonuclease activity for the multi-subunit tRNA splicing endonuclease complex.
source: Sen2 provides endonuclease activity for the multi-subunit tRNA splicing endonuclease complex and also cleaves a mitochondria-targeted non-stop mRNA (Ho et al., 1990; Tsuboi et al., 2015; Winey and Culbertson, 1988).
evidence: The text cites studies establishing Sen2's endonuclease function.

claim: Sen2 cleaves a mitochondria-targeted non-stop mRNA.
source: Sen2 provides endonuclease activity for the multi-subunit tRNA splicing endonuclease complex and also cleaves a mitochondria-targeted non-stop mRNA (Ho et al., 1990; Tsuboi et al., 2015; Winey and Culbertson, 1988).
evidence: The text cites studies showing Sen2's role in cleaving non-stop mRNA.

claim: The tRNA splicing complex resides on the MOM in yeast.
source: The tRNA splicing complex resides on the MOM in yeast, with Sen2 potentially anchoring it to the membrane via a hydrophobic segment (Trotta et al., 1997; Yoshihisa et al., 2003).
evidence: The text cites studies showing the localization of the tRNA splicing complex to the MOM.

claim: sam35-2ts and sen2-1ts encode full-length proteins.
source: We first determined that sam35-2ts and sen2-1ts encoded full-length proteins.
evidence: The text states this was determined experimentally.

claim: sam35-2ts and sen2-1ts contain multiple missense mutations.
source: Each contained multiple missense mutations (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A) that likely account for the phenotypes reported (Li et al., 2011; Milenkovic et al., 2004; Winey and Culbertson, 1988).
evidence: The text refers to Figure 1—figure supplement 1A showing the mutations and cites previous studies on the phenotypes.

claim: Genome-integrated versions of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts support cell viability at 25°C but not 37°C.
source: Genome-integrated versions of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts support cell viability at the permissive (25°C) but not non-permissive temperature (37°C; Figure 1A), consistent with the previously-described untagged versions (Li et al., 2011; Milenkovic et al., 2004; Winey and Culbertson, 1988).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 1A and cites previous studies.

claim: Increasing the temperature to 37°C results in dramatic destabilization of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts relative to WT proteins.
source: We find that increasing the temperature to 37°C results in dramatic destabilization of the ts- proteins relative to the WT proteins (Figure 1B).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 1B.

claim: sam35-2GFPts and sen2-1GFPts remain mitochondrially-associated after temperature increase to 37°C.
source: Co-expression of sam35-2GFPts and sen2-1GFPts with a mitochondrial marker (mtRFP) demonstrated that the ts- proteins remain mitochondrial after the temperature increase (Figure 1C).
evidence: The text describes microscopy results shown in Figure 1C.

claim: sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts fractionate almost exclusively to the mitochondrial pellet at 37°C.
source: Consistent with our microscopy, sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts fractionated almost exclusively to the mitochondrial pellet at 37°C (P; Figure 1D).
evidence: The text describes fractionation results shown in Figure 1D.

claim: sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts are destabilized at the non-permissive temperature yet remain mitochondrially-localized.
source: Therefore, sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts are destabilized at the non-permissive temperature yet remain mitochondrially-localized, validating their use as model MAD QC substrates.
evidence: The text summarizes experimental findings from multiple experiments.

claim: sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts are substantially stabilized in pre1-1 pre2-2 proteasome mutants.
source: The turnover of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts was assessed at the non-permissive temperature in strains containing conditional mutations in the 20S core (pre1-1 pre2-2; Figure 2A) or the 19S cap (cim3-1; Figure 2B) of the 26S proteasome. Both ts- proteins were substantially stabilized in these mutants relative to isogenic WT strains.
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figures 2A and 2B.

claim: sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts are substantially stabilized in cim3-1 proteasome mutants.
source: The turnover of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts was assessed at the non-permissive temperature in strains containing conditional mutations in the 20S core (pre1-1 pre2-2; Figure 2A) or the 19S cap (cim3-1; Figure 2B) of the 26S proteasome. Both ts- proteins were substantially stabilized in these mutants relative to isogenic WT strains.
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figures 2A and 2B.

claim: Vacuolar proteases are not required for sam35-2HAts or sen2-1HAts turnover.
source: In contrast, vacuolar or mitochondrial resident proteases were not required for sam35-2HAts or sen2-1HAts turnover (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Mitochondrial resident proteases are not required for sam35-2HAts or sen2-1HAts turnover.
source: In contrast, vacuolar or mitochondrial resident proteases were not required for sam35-2HAts or sen2-1HAts turnover (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts primarily accumulate at the mitochondria when their proteasomal degradation is blocked.
source: Even after 40 min at the non-permissive temperature, the majority of both sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts accumulated in the 12,000xg mitochondrial pellet (Figure 2C).
evidence: The text describes fractionation results shown in Figure 2C.

claim: sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts are peripheral membrane proteins.
source: Extraction of both proteins from this pellet fraction by sodium carbonate excluded the possibility that this represents aggregated protein (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The text describes sodium carbonate extraction results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C, which is a standard method to distinguish peripheral from integral membrane proteins.

claim: Purified mitochondrial fraction retains ~70% of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts.
source: On the other hand, this purified mitochondrial fraction retains ~70% of the ts- proteins.
evidence: The text describes quantification of fractionation results.

claim: sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts are stabilized in uba1-204 mutant.
source: Consistent with being UPS substrates, stabilization of both sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts was observed in a ts- mutant of the ubiquitin-activating enzyme (uba1-204; Figure 2D; Ghaboosi and Deshaies, 2007), indicating that ubiquitination is required for their degradation.
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 2D and cites a study on the uba1-204 mutant.

claim: Ubiquitin-modified forms of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts are evident when proteasome function is inhibited.
source: Moreover, ubiquitin-modified forms of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts were evident when proteasome function was inhibited (Figure 2E and F and see Figure 2—figure supplement 1F for an additional control), as indicated by characteristic higher molecular weight bands and a smear representing highly ubiquitinated species (Emmerich and Cohen, 2015).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figures 2E and F and cites a study on ubiquitin visualization.

claim: Ubiquitinated forms of WT SAM35HA and SEN2HA are much less prevalent than the ts- versions.
source: By comparison, ubiquitinated forms of WT SAM35HA and SEN2HA are much less prevalent (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1G.

claim: Ubiquitinated sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts both accumulated largely in the mitochondrial pellet fraction under conditions of proteasome impairment.
source: Ubiquitinated sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts both accumulated largely in the mitochondrial pellet fraction (P12,000xg; Figure 2—figure supplement 1H) and to a lesser extent in the soluble fraction, correlating with the relative distributions of unmodified species.
evidence: The text describes fractionation results shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1H.

claim: Ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation are required for the turnover of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts at the MOM.
source: Taken together, these data establish roles for ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation in the turnover of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts at the MOM.
evidence: The text summarizes experimental findings from multiple experiments.

claim: SCFMdm30 and Rsp5 are the only ubiquitin ligases known to act on mitochondrial proteins in yeast.
source: To date, the only ubiquitin ligases known to act on mitochondrial proteins in yeast are SCFMdm30 and Rsp5 (Belgareh-Touzé et al., 2017; Cohen et al., 2008; Escobar-Henriques et al., 2006; Kowalski et al., 2018; Wu et al., 2016).
evidence: The text cites multiple studies establishing these E3s as acting on mitochondrial proteins.

claim: Mdm30 and Rsp5 do not affect sam35-2HAts or sen2-1HAts stability.
source: We assessed whether these E3s also play a role in MAD of QC substrates and found that strains lacking either Mdm30 or Rsp5 function did not affect sam35-2HAts or sen2-1HAts stability (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: san1Δ impairs turnover of sam35-2HAts.
source: Interestingly, we found that san1Δ impaired turnover of sam35-2HAts (Figure 3A, middle panel), while ubr1Δ impaired turnover of sen2-1HAts (Figure 3B, middle panel).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 3A.

claim: ubr1Δ impairs turnover of sen2-1HAts.
source: Interestingly, we found that san1Δ impaired turnover of sam35-2HAts (Figure 3A, middle panel), while ubr1Δ impaired turnover of sen2-1HAts (Figure 3B, middle panel).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 3B.

claim: San1 has been implicated in QC of cytosolic and nuclear proteins.
source: San1 has been implicated in QC of cytosolic and nuclear proteins (Gardner et al., 2005; Heck et al., 2010).
evidence: The text cites studies establishing San1's role in QC.

claim: Ubr1 is the E3 that ubiquitinates N-end rule substrates.
source: Ubr1 is the E3 that ubiquitinates N-end rule substrates, but also plays a prominent role in the turnover of cytosolic proteins and, in some instances, may also degrade ER proteins (Bartel et al., 1990; Comyn et al., 2016; Eisele and Wolf, 2008; Heck et al., 2010; Khosrow-Khavar et al., 2012; Rao et al., 2001; Scazzari et al., 2015; Stolz et al., 2013; Summers et al., 2013).
evidence: The text cites multiple studies establishing Ubr1's roles.

claim: Loss of Ubr1 in conjunction with san1Δ leads to greater stabilization of sam35-2HAts than loss of San1 alone.
source: While ubr1Δ alone did not affect sam35-2HAts turnover (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C), loss of Ubr1 in conjunction with san1Δ led to greater stabilization than loss of San1 alone (Figure 3A, lower panel), indicating that Ubr1 can target sam35-2HAts in the absence of San1.
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Loss of San1, alone or in conjunction with ubr1Δ, does not affect the stability of sen2-1HAts.
source: Loss of San1, alone or in conjunction with ubr1Δ, did not affect the stability of sen2-1HAts (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D and Figure 3B, lower panel).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The polyubiquitination of sam35-2HAts is greatly reduced when San1 is deleted.
source: Notably, the polyubiquitination of sam35-2HAts (Figure 3C) and sen2-1HAts (Figure 3D) was greatly reduced when San1 or Ubr1, respectively, were deleted.
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The polyubiquitination of sen2-1HAts is greatly reduced when Ubr1 is deleted.
source: Notably, the polyubiquitination of sam35-2HAts (Figure 3C) and sen2-1HAts (Figure 3D) was greatly reduced when San1 or Ubr1, respectively, were deleted.
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Loss of Ubc4 stabilizes sen2-1HAts to a similar degree as ubr1Δ.
source: Loss of Ubc4, an E2 known to function with Ubr1 for select substrates, stabilized sen2-1HAts to a similar degree as ubr1Δ (Figure 3E).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 3E.

claim: sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts still accumulate almost exclusively in the pellet fraction in san1Δ and ubr1Δ, respectively.
source: To confirm that Ubr1 and San1 can act on ts- proteins at the MOM, we examined the localization of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts by fractionation in san1Δ and ubr1Δ, respectively. In these strains, both ts- proteins still accumulated almost exclusively in the pellet fraction (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: The text describes fractionation results shown in Figures 3F and G.

claim: San1 and Ubr1 function as components of the MAD machinery for proteasome-mediated degradation of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts, respectively.
source: These results establish that San1 and Ubr1 can function as components of the MAD machinery for proteasome-mediated degradation of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts, respectively.
evidence: The text summarizes experimental findings from multiple experiments.

claim: The cytosolic SSA family of Hsp70 chaperones is broadly involved in protein folding and refolding.
source: The cytosolic SSA family of Hsp70 chaperones (Ssa1, Ssa2, Ssa3, and Ssa4) is broadly involved in protein folding and refolding, but also plays a role in the degradation of several San1 and Ubr1 QC substrates (Guerriero et al., 2013; Heck et al., 2010; Prasad et al., 2010; Stolz et al., 2013).
evidence: The text cites multiple studies establishing SSA chaperones' roles.

claim: SSA chaperones play a role in the degradation of several San1 and Ubr1 QC substrates.
source: The cytosolic SSA family of Hsp70 chaperones (Ssa1, Ssa2, Ssa3, and Ssa4) is broadly involved in protein folding and refolding, but also plays a role in the degradation of several San1 and Ubr1 QC substrates (Guerriero et al., 2013; Heck et al., 2010; Prasad et al., 2010; Stolz et al., 2013).
evidence: The text cites multiple studies establishing SSA chaperones' roles in QC.

claim: SSA chaperones have not been implicated in MAD.
source: However, they have not been implicated in MAD.
evidence: The text states this as a gap in knowledge.

claim: Both sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts are strongly stabilized in ssa1-45ts mutant.
source: Interestingly, both sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts were strongly stabilized in a conditional yeast strain where three SSA family members are deleted and the fourth (SSA1) is ts- (ssa1-45ts; ssa1-45ts ssa2Δ ssa3Δ ssa4Δ) relative to the control strain (SSA1; SSA1 ssa2Δ ssa3Δ ssa4Δ; Figure 4A).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Both sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts are localized to the pellet fraction in ssa1-45ts mutant.
source: Both sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts were localized to the pellet fraction (Figure 4B), where they were extractable by sodium carbonate (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The text describes fractionation results shown in Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: SSA1 chaperone is required for ubiquitination of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts.
source: Notably, the SSA1 chaperone was also required for ubiquitination: despite the accumulation of unmodified sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts, ubiquitin-modified forms are dramatically reduced when SSA1 is inactivated (Figure 4C).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Degradation of Fzo1HA is largely unaffected by loss of SSA function.
source: In contrast to the ts- proteins, degradation of the native MOM UPS substrate, Fzo1HA, was largely unaffected by loss SSA function (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Depletion of ~90% of Sis1 protein slows the turnover of both sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts.
source: Depletion of ~90% of Sis1 protein using Sis1 DAmP cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C) slowed the turnover of both sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts (Figure 4D), while loss of Ydj1 or its ortholog, Hlj1, did not (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Loss of Ydj1 or Hlj1 does not affect turnover of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts.
source: Depletion of ~90% of Sis1 protein using Sis1 DAmP cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C) slowed the turnover of both sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts (Figure 4D), while loss of Ydj1 or its ortholog, Hlj1, did not (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Sse1 is not required for the degradation of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts.
source: We did not detect a role for Sse1 in the degradation of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Hsc82/Hsp82, Sti1, Hsp104, and Dsk2 are not required for the degradation of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts.
source: Loss of other factors implicated in San1 and Ubr1 nuclear import-dependent QC, including Hsc82/Hsp82, Sti1, Hsp104, and Dsk2 were also without effect on the degradation of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The degradation of mitochondrial QC substrates is dependent on both Hsp70 and Hsp40 chaperones, but independent of nuclear import.
source: These results establish that the degradation of the mitochondrial QC substrates is dependent on both Hsp70 and Hsp40 chaperones, but independent of nuclear import.
evidence: The text summarizes experimental findings from multiple experiments.

claim: Cdc48 plays a broad role in many QC pathways, generally functioning as a protein 'unfoldase' or 'segregase'.
source: The AAA-ATPase Cdc48 plays a broad role in many QC pathways, generally functioning as a protein 'unfoldase' or 'segregase,' while also maintaining protein solubility prior to proteasomal degradation (Neal et al., 2017; Ye et al., 2017).
evidence: The text cites studies establishing Cdc48's roles.

claim: Cdc48 and its co-factors Npl4 and Ufd1 have been implicated in the UPS-mediated turnover of several yeast MOM proteins.
source: Cdc48 and its co-factors Npl4 and Ufd1 have been implicated in the UPS-mediated turnover of several yeast MOM proteins (Cohen et al., 2008; Heo et al., 2010; Wu et al., 2016).
evidence: The text cites studies establishing Cdc48-Npl4-Ufd1's roles in MOM protein turnover.

claim: Both sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts are stabilized in conditional Cdc48, Npl4, and Ufd1 strains.
source: Both sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts were stabilized in conditional Cdc48, Npl4, and Ufd1 strains (Figure 5A).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Loss of Msp1 does not stabilize sam35-2HAts or sen2-1HAts.
source: In contrast, loss of Msp1, another AAA-ATPase that localizes to mitochondria and dislocates mislocalized tail-anchored proteins from the MOM (Chen et al., 2014; Okreglak and Walter, 2014; Wohlever et al., 2017), stabilized neither sam35-2HAts nor sen2-1HAts (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and cites studies on Msp1.

claim: sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts remain primarily mitochondrial in npl4-1 and ufd1-1 mutants.
source: For npl4-1 and ufd1-1, however, both substrates remain primarily mitochondrial (Figure 5B, middle and right panels).
evidence: The text describes fractionation results shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Ubiquitinated sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts increase in Cdc48-Npl4-Ufd1 complex mutants.
source: Accordingly, we detected a relative increase in ubiquitinated sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts in Cdc48-Npl4-Ufd1 complex mutants (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: Deletion of Rad23, Dsk2, or Ddi1 does not affect the degradation of sam35-2HAts or sen2-1HAts.
source: Deletion of these or another proteasome shuttling factor, Ddi1, did not affect the degradation of sam35-2HAts or sen2-1HAts (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D), further distinguishing MAD from ERAD.
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Ubiquitinated mitochondrial QC substrates require the Cdc48-Npl4-Ufd1 complex for efficient proteasomal degradation.
source: All together, these results indicate that ubiquitinated mitochondrial QC substrates require the Cdc48-Npl4-Ufd1 complex for efficient proteasomal degradation.
evidence: The text summarizes experimental findings from multiple experiments.

claim: Loss of Vms1 has no effect on the degradation of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts.
source: Loss of Vms1 had no effect on the degradation of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), while loss of Doa1 had a small, but significant effect (Figure 6A).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Loss of Doa1 has a small, but significant effect on the degradation of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts.
source: Loss of Vms1 had no effect on the degradation of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), while loss of Doa1 had a small, but significant effect (Figure 6A).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Loss of Ubx2 significantly stabilizes sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts.
source: Notably, only the loss of Ubx2 significantly stabilized sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Ubx2 is well-characterized as an ER membrane protein with roles in ERAD and lipid droplet homeostasis.
source: Ubx2 (as well as its mammalian ortholog, UbxD8) is well-characterized as an ER membrane protein with roles in ERAD and lipid droplet homeostasis (Kolawa et al., 2013; Neuber et al., 2005; Schuberth and Buchberger, 2005; Wang and Lee, 2012).
evidence: The text cites studies establishing Ubx2's roles.

claim: FLAG-tagged Ubx2 complements the degradation defect in ubx2Δ strain.
source: We confirmed Ubx2's role in degradation of the mitochondrial ts- proteins by complementation with FLAG-tagged Ubx2 in the ubx2Δ strain (Figure 6C).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Doa1 overexpression fails to restore sam35-2HAts or sen2-1HAts degradation in ubx2Δ cells.
source: Furthermore, redundant functions for Ubx2 and Doa1 were ruled out by a failure of Doa1 overexpression to restore sam35-2HAts or sen2-1HAts degradation in ubx2Δ cells (Figure 6D).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Ubiquitinated forms of ts- substrates accumulate in the absence of Ubx2.
source: As might be predicted given the role of Ubx2 in linking ubiquitinated proteins to the Cdc48 complex, ubiquitinated forms of the ts- substrates accumulated in the absence of Ubx2 (Figure 6E).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 6E.

claim: A physical association between Ubx2-FLAG and the ts- proteins was detected by co-immunoprecipitation.
source: We also detected a physical association between Ubx2-FLAG and the ts- proteins as assessed by co-immunoprecipitation (Figure 6F).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Loss of Ubx2 does not affect the turnover of SAM35HA or SEN2HA.
source: We see no evidence that loss of Ubx2 affects the already slow turnover of either SAM35HA or SEN2HA (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C), and an association between these WT proteins and Ubx2 was also not as pronounced relative to their abundance (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: Loss of Ubx2 and Doa1 stabilizes Fzo1HA.
source: However, in agreement with recent reports (Chowdhury et al., 2018; Nahar et al., 2020; Wu et al., 2016), we find that loss of Ubx2 and, to a lesser extent, Doa1, stabilizes Fzo1HA, which is a native MOM UPS substrate (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E and F).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1E and F and cites recent studies.

claim: Fzo1HA physically interacts with Ubx2.
source: Importantly, we also establish that Fzo1HA physically interacts with Ubx2, accompanied by an increase in ubiquitinated forms (Figure 6—figure supplement 1G and H).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1G and H.

claim: Ubx2 may also localize to mitochondria.
source: Although Ubx2 is an ER transmembrane protein, one study suggested it may also localize to mitochondria (Wang and Lee, 2012), which was recently corroborated (Mårtensson et al., 2019).
evidence: The text cites studies suggesting Ubx2 localization to mitochondria.

claim: Ubx2-GFP co-localizes with both ER and mitochondrial markers by microscopy.
source: We also confirmed this by co-localization of Ubx2-GFP with both ER (Sec63-RFP) and mitochondrial (mtRFP) markers by microscopy (Figure 6—figure supplement 1I).
evidence: The text describes microscopy results shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1I.

claim: A portion of Ubx2 localizes to mitochondria as verified biochemically by isolation of mitochondria.
source: The mitochondrial localization of a portion of Ubx2 was further verified biochemically by isolation of mitochondria largely devoid of co-purifying cytosolic (PGK), ER luminal (CPY), or ER membrane (Cue1) proteins (Figure 6G).
evidence: The text describes fractionation results shown in Figure 6G.

claim: The turnover of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts is unaffected in strains mutant for each of the four ERMES components.
source: The turnover of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts was unaffected in strains mutant for each of the four ERMES components (Figure 6—figure supplement 1J), indicating that significant reductions in ER-mitochondrial contact do not impair their degradation.
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1J.

claim: ts- protein degradation is unaffected by combined loss of the major ERAD E2s, Ubc6 and Ubc7.
source: Furthermore, ts- protein degradation is unaffected by combined loss of the major ERAD E2s, Ubc6 and Ubc7, or E3s, Doa10 and Hrd1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1K and L), with which Ubx2 functionally and physically interacts at the ER (Neuber et al., 2005; Schuberth and Buchberger, 2005).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1K and L and cites studies on Ubx2 interactions.

claim: ts- protein degradation is unaffected by combined loss of the major ERAD E3s, Doa10 and Hrd1.
source: Furthermore, ts- protein degradation is unaffected by combined loss of the major ERAD E2s, Ubc6 and Ubc7, or E3s, Doa10 and Hrd1 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1K and L), with which Ubx2 functionally and physically interacts at the ER (Neuber et al., 2005; Schuberth and Buchberger, 2005).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1K and L and cites studies on Ubx2 interactions.

claim: Degradation of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts is independent of Msp1.
source: Degradation of sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAtsis independent of Msp1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts largely accumulate in the mitochondrial pellet in ubx2Δ cells.
source: Sam35-2HAts and sen2-1HAts also largely accumulate in the mitochondrial pellet in ubx2Δ cells (Figure 6H).
evidence: The text describes fractionation results shown in Figure 6H.

claim: Degradation of Fzo1HA is unaffected by loss of ERMES components.
source: Similar to the ts- proteins, degradation of Fzo1HA, which is a substrate for the cytosolic E3 SCFMDM30 and its cognate E2 Cdc34 (Cohen et al., 2008), is unaffected by loss of ERMES components (Figure 6—figure supplement 1M).
evidence: The text describes experimental results shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1M and cites a study on Fzo1HA.

claim: Fzo1 accumulates predominantly in the mitochondrial pellet when Ubx2 is absent.
